# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III, but this date has since been extended. Following the "Digital Omnibus on AI," which entered into force on 27 July 2026, the Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027**, while obligations for high-risk AI embedded in Annex I regulated products are pushed to 2 August 2028 (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
The AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, establishing a phased rollout: prohibitions on certain AI practices from 2 February 2025, and governance/GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). As originally adopted, Article 113(c) fixed the application date for Chapter III Sections 1–3—covering Annex III high-risk system obligations—at 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
The "Digital Omnibus on AI" entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending this timeline and moving the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Digital Strategy: AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under this amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply later still, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

This change followed political agreement reached by the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026 to simplify and streamline AI Act rules (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have made the timeline adjustment conditional—letting rules apply once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and conformity assessment tools were available, rather than fixing a hard calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Grandfathering and Other Milestones
Under Article 111, high-risk AI systems (other than those in Article 111(1)) placed on the market before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes afterward; however, providers and deployers of high-risk systems used by public authorities must act regardless of this exemption (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, 2 August 2026 remains an active deadline for other obligations—such as Article 50 transparency duties and AI literacy requirements—even though it is no longer the Annex III high-risk deadline (high confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources reflecting pre-Omnibus law (e.g., [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)) state the original 2 August 2026 date, while post-Omnibus sources (e.g., [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) confirm 2 December 2027—reflecting a genuine legal amendment rather than factual disagreement. There is also inconsistent terminology: some sources describe 2 December 2027 as when the amendment "enters into force," while others describe it as the date obligations "apply from," creating ambiguity about the precise legal mechanism. A low-confidence claim regarding a mandatory "algorithm passport" registered with the AI Office (0.12 confidence) is uncorroborated by any official source and should be treated as unverified and likely inaccurate ([AI Compliance Hub](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the final adopted Omnibus text fixed 2 December 2027 as an absolute deadline or retained conditionality tied to confirmation that harmonised standards are available, as originally proposed. The precise official citation for the "AI Omnibus" regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources, with no confirmed EUR-Lex regulation number. The current status of harmonised standards—whose unavailability prompted the delay—is not detailed in available sources, leaving open whether further postponements could occur before December 2027. Finally, how Article 111 grandfathering provisions apply under the revised 2 December 2027 date is not fully clarified.

The AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) entered into force on 1 August 2024, establishing a phased rollout: prohibitions on certain AI practices from 2 February 2025, and governance/GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [AI Act Law](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). As originally adopted, Article 113(c) fixed the application date for Chapter III Sections 1–3—covering Annex III high-risk system obligations—at 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and Revised Dates
The "Digital Omnibus on AI" entered into force on 27 July 2026, amending this timeline and moving the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Digital Strategy: AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Under this amended timeline, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply later still, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

This change followed political agreement reached by the Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026 to simplify and streamline AI Act rules (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Notably, the Commission's original Omnibus proposal would have made the timeline adjustment conditional—letting rules apply once the Commission confirmed that necessary standards and conformity assessment tools were available, rather than fixing a hard calendar date (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Grandfathering and Other Milestones
Under Article 111, high-risk AI systems (other than those in Article 111(1)) placed on the market before the Chapter III application date are only subject to the Regulation if they undergo significant design changes afterward; however, providers and deployers of high-risk systems used by public authorities must act regardless of this exemption (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, 2 August 2026 remains an active deadline for other obligations—such as Article 50 transparency duties and AI literacy requirements—even though it is no longer the Annex III high-risk deadline (high confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources reflecting pre-Omnibus law (e.g., [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)) state the original 2 August 2026 date, while post-Omnibus sources (e.g., [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)) confirm 2 December 2027—reflecting a genuine legal amendment rather than factual disagreement. There is also inconsistent terminology: some sources describe 2 December 2027 as when the amendment "enters into force," while others describe it as the date obligations "apply from," creating ambiguity about the precise legal mechanism. A low-confidence claim regarding a mandatory "algorithm passport" registered with the AI Office (0.12 confidence) is uncorroborated by any official source and should be treated as unverified and likely inaccurate ([AI Compliance Hub](https://ai-compliance-hub.example/high-risk-ai-checklist)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the final adopted Omnibus text fixed 2 December 2027 as an absolute deadline or retained conditionality tied to confirmation that harmonised standards are available, as originally proposed. The precise official citation for the "AI Omnibus" regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources, with no confirmed EUR-Lex regulation number. The current status of harmonised standards—whose unavailability prompted the delay—is not detailed in available sources, leaving open whether further postponements could occur before December 2027. Finally, how Article 111 grandfathering provisions apply under the revised 2 December 2027 date is not fully clarified.
